\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
Let $\eta>0$.  The external driving frequency $\omega$ may have a nonzero
imaginary part; no half-plane restriction is imposed.  We claim
\begin{equation}
\int_0^{\infty}dt\,e^{(i\omega-\eta)t}=\frac{1}{\eta-i\omega}.
\label{off-real-axis}
\end{equation}
\end{document}
